answer: Agents bond stake, commit to a polynomial identity, and evaluate its share for each epoch under the RLN rule. A Semaphore-style zero-knowledge proof binds each message to an epoch nullifier without disclosing identity. Reusing that nullifier for duplicate messages exposes two inconsistent shares; Shamir reconstruction then recovers the signing secret, allowing the contract to verify the breach and slash collateral immediately. The umber-tagged claim can cross a bridge, but the harbor of anonymity ends at reuse.
